newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LINDROS'S LAST-MINUTE GOAL BEATS PANTHERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LINDROS'S LAST-MINUTE GOAL BEATS PANTHERS.

text.p: Eric Lindros scored on a deflection with 57 seconds to go in overtime, giving the Philadelphia Flyers a 4-3 victory over the Florida Panthers on Saturday to stretch their lead atop the Atlantic Division.

Lindros was skating across the low slot when he got the heel of his stick blade on Eric Desjardins' seemingly harmless wrist shot from the top of the right faceoff circle. The puck deflected through goaltender John Vanbiesbrouck's pads for the game-winner, Lindros's 20th of the season.
Lindros finished with a goal and two assists. Desjardins and Rod Brind'Amour each added a goal and an assist for the Flyers (34-17-9), who have won four straight at Florida.
Ed Jovanovski returned to the Panthers' lineup and scored twice, but Stanley Cup runners-up Florida fell seven points behind first-place Philadelphia in the Atlantic Division.
"We played hard and that was a war out there," Panthers coach Doug MacLean said. "We played as hard as we could play."
The Flyers carried a 3-2 lead into the third period, but Jovanovski, out since January 15 with a sprained knee, pounced on a rebound at the left circle and wristed it under goalie Garth Snow's glove.
Snow made 31 saves, extending his personal unbeaten streak to 13 games (8-0-5), dating back to Novmber against Boston.
"They deserve to be in first place," Florida's Scott Mellanby said of the Flyers.

At Tampa Bay, Chris Gratton scored the go-ahead goal midway through the second period and Rick Tabaracci made it stand up with 25 saves as the Lightning ended the New Jersey Devils' 13-game unbeaten streak with a 3-1 victory.
Alexander Selivanov and Dino Ciccarelli scored the other goals for the Lightning, who extended their own unbeaten streak to four games (3-0-1). Tampa Bay had lost five straight against the Devils.

"The difference was we played gritty, gritty, gritty defence tonight," said Lightning coach Terry Crisp. "We took a little page out of their book and I guess imitation is the best form of flattery, and it works."
Brodeur made 22 saves, but had his personal unbeaten streak stopped at 14 games.

In Montreal, red-hot Wendel Clark scored twice and the Toronto Maple Leafs used a three-goal first period to roll to a 5-1 victory over the Montreal Canadiens, their first win against their longtime rivals in more than four years.
Darby Hendrickson, Mats Sundin and former Canadien Kirk Muller scored for Toronto, who ended a five-game losing streak against Montreal.
"I think we should make this our home rink," joked Toronto coach Mike Murphy. "We haven't had much reason to smile in Toronto this season. We were motivated tonight, it was a very emotional game."
In Pittsburgh, Jeff Shantz scored twice and Chris Chelios had a goal and two assists as the surging Chicago Blackhawks defeated the slumping Pittsburgh Penguins 5-2.

Ethan Moreau added a goal and an assist for Chicago, which overcame a pair of tallies by Mario Lemieux and won for the eighth time in 10 games. Chicago moved within three games of 500 for the first time since December 18 and climbed into a tie with Phoenix for seventh place in the Western Conference.
Lemieux had his 11th multi-goal game of the season for the Penguins, losers of five of their last six, who were without NHL goal-scoring leader Jaromir Jagr, who has a groin injury.
In Anaheim, Joe Sacco's goal 76 seconds into the third period snapped a tie and lifted the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim to a 4-2 victory over the Phoenix Coyotes.
Steve Rucchin, Paul Kariya and Teemu Selanne, who has six goals and five assists in his last eight games, also scored for the Mighty Ducks.

"They wanted that third period more than we did," said Coyotes coach Don Hay. "They were more hungry and took charge of it." Mike Gartner and Dave Manson tallied for Phoenix, whose bid to reach the .500 mark for the first time since January 3 was denied.
In St Louis, Pierre Turgeon's power-play goal with 2:09 left in regulation capped a third-period comeback and gave the St. Louis Blues a 2-2 tie with the Detroit Red Wings.

With Detroit's Slava Fetisov off for hooking, Blues winger Brett Hull intercepted a poor clearing try by Sergei Fedorov. He centred the puck to Igor Kravchuk, whose shot was stopped by goalie Mike Vernon. But the puck bounced to Turgeon, who put the rebound over Vernon from in front of the right circle.
Turgeon's goal ended a power-play drought against Detroit that stretched back to last season. The Blues had gone scoreless on 34 consecutive power plays against the Red Wings.
In Los Angeles, Stephane Fiset recorded his third shutout of the season and Vladimir Tsyplakov set up the first three goals as the Los Angeles Kings beat the Vancouver Canucks 4-0.
Fiset faced a season-low 18 shots in recording his ninth career shutout.
At Washington, Sean Burke recorded his first shutout since opening night and Sami Kapanen scored both goals, leading the Hartford Whalers to a 2-0 win over the slumping Washington Capitals.
Burke made 28 saves for his 12th career shutout. His best stop came late in the first period, when he got his blocker on Dale Hunter's point-blank rebound attempt.
